t: The mission had been more difficult than Kai Krellis would have believed when he started. Finally though, the end was in sight. He had seen how priestesses could carve through masses of undead, and now he traveled with a whole contingent of them. Tyegëa was even more powerful, though as unpredictable as Cylanna had said.

The tribe that had fled Jotha unable to fight returned as an army stiffened by veteran fighters and led by a warrior king. Though they were tired from their journey, weariness fell from them as they neared home. The merfolk arrived during the night, and found the mouth of their bay guarded, so they headed south along the coast to some outlying villages to gather news of the invaders.
The bat slips the ring over a claw, and flies straight up, flapping powerfully.
The ring of power increases the damage of all its owner’s attacks by one, and adds three hitpoints.
We will let the bat have the ring. It will make him more helpful.
Someone take that off him before he hurts himself.
I feel different, and all my weapons are lighter!
The ring of power increases the damage of all its owner’s attacks by one, and adds three hitpoints.
I’ll take this ring, and you can rely on my strength.
This thing makes me dizzy. Someone else can have it.
Killing these enemies was good, but there are many more on the way. I’m sure it is still unsafe here.
I agree. I hate to leave our home, but we will return.

t: Loyal units don’t incur upkeep. Most units incur an upkeep cost at the end of every turn, which is equal to their level. Loyal units do not incur this cost.

During campaigns, certain units may opt to join the player’s forces of their own volition. These units are marked with the loyal trait. Although they may require payment to be recalled, they never incur any upkeep costs. This can make them invaluable during a long campaign, when gold is in short supply. This trait is never given to recruited units, so it may be unwise to dismiss such units or to send them to a foolish death.
Resilient units have an additional 4 hitpoints, and gain 1 more per level.

Resilient units can be useful at all stages of a campaign, and this is a useful trait for all units. Resilient is often most helpful as a trait when it occurs in a unit that has some combination of low hitpoints, good defense, or high resistances. Resilient units are especially useful for holding strategic positions against opponents.
Loyal units don’t incur upkeep. Most units incur an upkeep cost at the end of every turn, which is equal to their level. Loyal units do not incur this cost.

During campaigns, certain units may opt to join the player’s forces of their own volition. These units are marked with the loyal trait. Although they may require payment to be recalled, they never incur any upkeep costs. This can make them invaluable during a long campaign, when gold is in short supply. This trait is never given to recruited units, so it may be unwise to dismiss such units or to send them to a foolish death.
Intelligent units require 20% less experience than usual to advance.

Intelligent units are very useful at the beginning of a campaign as they can advance to higher levels more quickly. Later in campaigns Intelligent is not quite as useful because the After Maximum Level Advancement (AMLA) is not as significant a change as advancing a level. If you have many ‘maximum level’ units you may wish to recall units with more desirable traits.
Loyal units don’t incur upkeep. Most units incur an upkeep cost at the end of every turn, which is equal to their level. Loyal units do not incur this cost.

During campaigns, certain units may opt to join the player’s forces of their own volition. These units are marked with the loyal trait. Although they may require payment to be recalled, they never incur any upkeep costs. This can make them invaluable during a long campaign, when gold is in short supply. This trait is never given to recruited units, so it may be unwise to dismiss such units or to send them to a foolish death.
Strong units do 1 more damage for every successful strike in melee combat, and have 1 additional hitpoint.

While useful for any close-combat unit, strong is most effective for units who have a high number of swings such as the elvish fighter. Strong units can be very useful when a tiny bit of extra damage is all that is needed to turn a damaging stroke into a killing blow.
Kai Krellis! You live! We thought you and your people had all been killed when Jotha fell.
No, most of us escaped. I thought your settlements might be far enough away to escape harm, but you look as if you had seen battle.

Indeed, though we have not been hard-pressed. The creatures have been busy fouling the waters and making the bay more to their liking. We worry that they will soon be back to finish with us, and I fear we will not survive.
We come prepared for battle, and have brought help. We will reclaim our home and make yours safe as well. Mal-Ravanal will pay this day.

Good. We will join you. You will be impressed with how quickly Tabomo here crushes skeletons. I think we should make the ruined castle on the mainland our base. The undead cut down many trees there to make bridges, and it is much easier to move through now.
At dawn, the merfolk got a good look at their opponents.
Maybe not yet, but just wait.
The merfolk...they came back! Bring back the search parties! Call back the hordes!
Just make some more, you fool. There are plenty of corpses to go around.
I suppose this does look a little overwhelming. I may enjoy it though. It can be satisfying to rain holy fire down on misbehaving spirits.
We searched up the coast for miles, and here they are!
I was wrong. You are no grandson of mine!
The human wizard was wearing a ring! Maybe it is magic. Someone should try it on to see what it does.
The human wizard was wearing a ring! Maybe it is magic. Someone should try it on to see what it does.
Inky has found something. Someone should check it out.
Something must be there! Good bat! Someone should find out what it is.
This man was wearing a necklace with a pendant on it. I’m sure the shape means something.
It does indeed. It is an ankh, and that pendant will strengthen your life force.
The ankh necklace provides 70% resistance to arcane damage.
That sounds great! I’ll take it.
It doesn’t seem to have helped its previous owner. I don’t want it.
I would like my life force protected.
My life force feels fine as it is.
